E1.evidence: Issue #5386 gives the full parameter file, reproduction steps and the observed effect ("On Ubuntu 24.04, maximum speed is limited to \~0.25 m/s."), with the installed version "ros-jazzy-navigation2 1.3.7-1noble.20250624.020544". The merged jazzy backport PR #6336 names #5386 and states the mechanism: "Fixes a Humble to Jazzy regression: MPPI seeds rollouts from lagging odometry instead of its own last command".

E2.evidence: Step 1: the MPPI controller plugin (loaded in controller_server, which reads the robot twist from odom_topic "/odometry/filtered" through nav_2d_utils::OdomSubscriber and passes it to the plugin) and the separately deployed process that publishes that odometry. Step 2: the failure depends on a timing assumption across that boundary: at 1.3.7 the optimizer sets state_.speed = robot_speed and seeds the rollouts' initial velocity from it (updateInitialStateVelocities), with per-step acceleration limits max_delta_vx = model_dt * ax_max applied after it, so an odometry twist that lags the commanded velocity caps the achievable speed. The maintainer states the cross-unit assumption in #5214: "all controllers in Nav2 assume that your robot has properly setup robot controllers to be able to execute commands given." A peer whose reported twist tracked the command would not trigger it. Step 3/4: the resolving change adds a new controller parameter and changes the optimizer's use of the consumed twist; not wiring or build only.

E3.evidence: PAIR: the odometry source's /odometry/filtered output feeds the controller's initial-state input. The symptom surfaced on the reporter's Humble-to-Jazzy migration (the whole stack moved from Ubuntu 22.04/Humble to 24.04/Jazzy), but the odometry provider is not identified as upgraded against a fixed consumer, so the failure is recorded in the pairing; see notes.

E4.evidence: Observed wrong motion: "On Ubuntu 24.04, maximum speed is limited to \~0.25 m/s." (issue #5386).

units.name: nav2_mppi_controller
units.revision_basis: The reporter lists "ros-jazzy-navigation2 1.3.7-1noble.20250624.020544"; tag 1.3.7 (803e7b81089d196c53593b1d5aec9020f1659f9d, 2025-05-30) is the source of that binary release. The resolving change is the jazzy backport merge commit 3f71f94b105b6731953a137561e8c27acc3e3acf (PR #6336, merged 2026-08-11); the first jazzy tag containing it is 1.3.13 (f4108e5b), tag 1.3.12 does not contain it. The fix is opt-in (open_loop defaults to false).

units.name: robot_odometry_source
units.revision_basis: The reporter never identifies the process that publishes "/odometry/filtered" (conventionally a robot_localization EKF over the robot's wheel odometry) nor its version; the resolution does not change it, so it keeps its as-reported label.

failed_conditions.quote: Fixes a Humble to Jazzy regression: MPPI seeds rollouts from lagging odometry instead of its own last command

loudness_evidence: "On Ubuntu 24.04, maximum speed is limited to \~0.25 m/s." (https://github.com/ros-navigation/navigation2/issues/5386); no diagnostic is reported, the reporter found it by observing /cmd_vel.

resolution.summary: Add an MPPI parameter open_loop (default false); when true, Optimizer::prepare seeds state_.speed from the controller's own last command (last_command_vel_) instead of the odometry twist, and reset() zeroes that stored command. Upstream PR #5617 (main, merge 8dbc92910b020b19b9891849b3ee7cb92e1b3b03), backported to jazzy as PR #6336 (merge 3f71f94b105b6731953a137561e8c27acc3e3acf).
resolution.evidence: Not shown working in the reporter's composition: the reporter closed the issue after concluding "It seems that the small acceleration value causes the vehicle to slow down." The backport author reports it working with a different peer: "Tested: Ubuntu 24.04, MuJoCo sim. Our measurement on a simulated Ridgeback mecanum base, vx_max: 0.5: commanded speed 0.165 to 0.466 m/s; ground truth 0.138 to 0.452" (https://github.com/ros-navigation/navigation2/pull/6336).

notes: Class 'other' is used because the mismatch is a latency of the consumed twist relative to the commanded velocity (a timing assumption), which none of the listed classes (rate_shortfall covers publishing rate, qos_deadline an enforced QoS policy) describes. The reporter's own diagnosis differs in emphasis: the acceleration limits ax_max/ax_min/ay_*/az_max in their YAML were ignored on Humble (the humble branch optimizer declares no ax_max) and take effect on Jazzy ("I think the following parameters are not effective in the HUMBLE version ... and it is effective in JAZZY"); another user worked around it by raising ax_max to 15.0. The maintainer first pointed to the migration guides and a missing velocity smoother. The fix PR in the packet attributes the regression to seeding from lagging odometry and cites #5386 and #5694 (0.17 m/s cap after migration) as the same symptom class; #5214 is the upstream discussion (motor lag with heavy load), where an earlier change (#5266) was merged then reverted. The symptom appeared with a Humble-to-Jazzy migration of the whole stack, so an UPGRADE reading of nav2_mppi_controller is also possible, but the second unit in that reading would be the reporter's own parameter file, which is configuration of the same node rather than a separate unit. The odometry provider (and the base driver that consumes /cmd_vel, whose response lag produces the lagging twist) is not identified by the reporter; /cmd_vel is therefore left out of the inventory. The artifact section for robot_odometry_source is empty because the source quotes no code, definition, or interface-attribute statement for it.
